title: How High-Net-Worth Families Can Protect Wealth for the Next Generation | Dimensional
gist: Episode 54 of Dimensional's 'The Informed Investor' podcast, featuring Mark Gochnour (Head of Global Client Services Group), argues that high-net-worth families protect generational wealth less through the plan itself than through early, iterative, and transparent communication of that plan to family members.

insights.claim: High-net-worth families should start family wealth governance discussions with heirs as early as possible rather than deferring the conversation until a death, incapacity, or other forcing event.
insights.speaker: Mark Gochnour
insights.so_what: Wealth advisors and family offices should treat early governance conversations as a core deliverable, not an optional add-on, when onboarding or retaining HNW clients.
insights.quote: Get started on family wealth governance discussions as soon as possible.

insights.claim: Family wealth governance works best as an iterative process where each family meeting builds on progress made at prior meetings, rather than a single one-time disclosure event.
insights.speaker: Mark Gochnour
insights.so_what: Advisors structuring succession plans should design a recurring meeting cadence rather than a single estate-planning session, improving continuity and reducing family conflict at transfer time.
insights.quote: Build on the progress of those discussions at successive meetings.

insights.claim: Wealth holders should proactively share age-appropriate financial information with family members instead of keeping wealth details secret from heirs until succession occurs.
insights.speaker: Mark Gochnour
insights.so_what: This pushes against the common HNW practice of withholding financial details from children; advisors can differentiate by offering structured, age-tiered disclosure frameworks as a service.
insights.quote: Don’t hesitate to share age-appropriate information with family members.

insights.claim: Having a formal wealth plan is treated as necessary but insufficient for protecting generational wealth — the plan must also be actively communicated to and understood by the family it is meant to protect.
insights.speaker: Mark Gochnour
insights.so_what: Wealth transfer failure risk is framed as a communication problem as much as a planning problem, implying advisory value shifts toward facilitating family dialogue, not just drafting documents.
insights.quote: Do you have a plan for your wealth? And, if so, are you prepared to share that plan with your family?
insights.locator: Episode 54 of The Informed Investor podcast

source_meta.author: Featuring Mark Gochnour, Head of Global Client Services Group
